summary.en: Venezuela is coping with deadly earthquakes that have killed thousands and prompted humanitarian response, while President Nicolás Maduro and his wife have pleaded not guilty to U.S. conspiracy to torture charges and face a trial in New York. The United States has deployed Space Force electromagnetic and electronic warfare systems against Venezuela and disclosed use of space warfare weapons, mirroring actions taken in Iran, and is preparing to justify recent boat strikes on drug traffickers near Venezuelan waters. A U.S. soldier who wagered $400,000 on Maduro's removal made his first court appearance and was arrested. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Venezuela takler dødelige jordskjelv som har drept tusenvis og utløst humanitær respons, mens president Nicolás Maduro og hans kone har erklært seg uskyldige i amerikanske konspirasjonsanklager om tortur og står overfor en rettssak i New York. USA har satt inn Space Force-systemer for elektromagnetisk og elektronisk krigføring mot Venezuela og offentliggjort bruk av romkrigsvåpen, i likhet med tiltakene mot Iran, og forbereder å rettferdiggjøre nylige båtangrep på narkotikasmuglere nær Venezuelas farvann. En amerikansk soldat som satset 400 000 dollar på Maduros avsettelse, møtte i første rettsmøte og ble arrestert. To dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
